subject: Admit it, Minister. Then apologise.
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

You wrote the powers. You direct the department that uses them. And farmers across Victoria have been on the receiving end of it.

Your staff have turned up unannounced and tried to get onto farms that never invited them. In one case they brought security with them to lean on a farmer in his eighties about VNI West.

And when Greg Baldwin rang triple zero to report trespassers on his own land, it was Baldwin who ended up charged. On 27 April 2026 the Director of Public Prosecutions withdrew every single charge. Not some of them. All of them.

So I am asking you for three things, and I am asking in writing so there is a record of it.

Admit that you directed your department to target farmers.

Apologise to the farming families you put through it.

Come clean, and stop.

Farming families are not an obstacle to be managed. We are the people who feed this state.

Yours sincerely,

subject: You built these powers. Now own what they did.
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

The access powers being used against Victorian farmers did not appear by accident. They were legislated, and you are the Minister responsible for the department applying them.

That department has attempted access on farms right across this state without invitation. Farmers have described staff arriving with security to press an elderly landholder about VNI West. Greg Baldwin called triple zero over trespassers on his own farm and was charged for it, until the DPP withdrew every charge on 27 April 2026.

This is not a run of bad luck. It is a pattern, and it runs through your portfolio.

I want three things from you, in writing.

Admit you directed your department to target farmers.

Apologise to the families it was done to.

Stop it.

Yours sincerely,

subject: An 80-year-old and a security escort. Explain that.
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

Farmers have told us your department turned up to talk to a man in his eighties about VNI West and brought security staff along to do it.

Think about what that says. A department under your direction decided an elderly farmer on his own land needed to be met with muscle.

That is not consultation. That is intimidation, and it is not isolated. Access has been attempted on farms across Victoria that never asked for a visit. Greg Baldwin rang triple zero about trespassers on his own farm and was charged, with every charge withdrawn by the DPP on 27 April 2026.

Admit you directed this. Apologise to the families who wore it. Then stop.

I would like your answer in writing.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Come clean about what your department has been doing
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

I am writing about how your department has treated Victorian farmers.

Farms across this state have had staff arrive uninvited and attempt to get onto private land. At least one elderly farmer was approached with security in tow over VNI West. And Greg Baldwin, who called triple zero to report trespassers on his own property, was the one charged, until the DPP withdrew every charge on 27 April 2026.

I do not accept that this happened without direction. Departments follow ministers.

So: admit you directed your department to target farmers. Apologise to the families affected. Come clean and stop.

Three sentences from you would settle all of it. I would like them in writing.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Farmers are owed an apology, Minister
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

Somewhere in your portfolio a decision was taken that Victorian farmers were an obstacle to be pushed through rather than people to be dealt with straight.

The result: uninvited attempts to access farms across the state, an elderly landholder approached with security over VNI West, and Greg Baldwin charged after ringing triple zero about trespassers on his own farm. The DPP withdrew every charge on 27 April 2026.

Those families are owed an apology from the Minister responsible, not a media statement about the energy transition.

Admit you directed it. Apologise. Stop.

Yours sincerely,

subject: He rang triple zero. He got charged. You're responsible.
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

Greg Baldwin did what any of us would do. He saw people on his land who had no business being there and he rang triple zero.

He was the one charged. On 27 April 2026 the Director of Public Prosecutions withdrew every charge against him. There was never a case.

He is not the only one. Farms across Victoria have had uninvited attempts at access, and farmers have described your department bringing security to press an elderly landholder about VNI West.

You built the powers and you direct the department. Admit you directed your department to target farmers, apologise to the families, and stop.

In writing, please.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Three generations on this land. Then your department arrived.
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

Farming families in this state have worked the same country for three and four generations. They have dealt with drought, fire and flood without asking anyone for special treatment.

What they did not expect was their own government coming at them: staff attempting access on farms that never invited them, security brought along to press an elderly farmer about VNI West, and Greg Baldwin charged for ringing triple zero about trespassers on his own land before the DPP withdrew every charge on 27 April 2026.

You are the Minister. Admit you directed your department to target farmers. Apologise to those families. Then stop.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Your silence is becoming the admission, Minister
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

You have had ample opportunity to explain how Victorian farmers came to be treated this way by your department, and you have not taken it.

Uninvited attempts at access on farms across the state. Security brought to a conversation with a farmer in his eighties about VNI West. Greg Baldwin charged after calling triple zero about trespassers on his own farm, with every charge withdrawn by the DPP on 27 April 2026.

Saying nothing does not make it go away. It just tells farming families you are content with what was done in your name.

Admit you directed it. Apologise. Stop.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Farmers are afraid to call the police now. That's on you.
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

There are farmers in this state who now think twice about ringing the police when strangers turn up on their land, because of what happened to Greg Baldwin. He made that call. He was the one charged. The DPP withdrew every charge on 27 April 2026.

That is what your department's conduct has produced, along with uninvited attempts at access on farms across Victoria and security brought along to press an elderly farmer about VNI West.

You wrote the powers and you direct the department. Admit you directed your department to target farmers, apologise to the families, and stop.

Yours sincerely,

subject: Stop targeting farmers, Minister
body:
Dear Minister D'Ambrosio,

I am one of many Victorians writing to you about the same thing, and I will keep it short.

Your department has attempted access on farms across this state that never invited it. Farmers have described staff arriving with security to lean on an elderly landholder about VNI West. Greg Baldwin was charged for ringing triple zero about trespassers on his own farm, and on 27 April 2026 the DPP withdrew every charge.

You legislated the powers. You direct the department.

Admit you directed your department to target farmers.

Apologise to every farming family you put through it.

Come clean, and stop.

Yours sincerely,
